title: Sheafification of a finite-projective affine section comparison
statement: Let $Y$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and put $A=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$. Let $D$ be a cochain complex of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with quasi-coherent terms. Let $P$ be a cochain complex of finite projective $A$-modules and let $q:P\to\Gamma(Y,D)$ be a quasi-isomorphism of the actual complexes. Define $C$ by termwise associated sheaves followed by restriction along the canonical isomorphism $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. Each $C^n$ is quasi-coherent, finitely presented and flat over the identity of $Y$ [def-pc-morphism-conventions], and there exists a quasi-isomorphism $e:C\to D$. There are no bounds or perfectness hypotheses.

source.place: Tags 01IB (schemes-lemma-spec-sheaves) and 08EB (perfect-lemma-perfect-affine); affine sectionwise flatness as in Tags 01I9 and 00HT

proof.text: Apply exact associated sheaves and restriction along the affine chart to q. Apply the quasi-coherent counit to each term of D; its naturality in the differentials yields a chain isomorphism from the associated ordinary section complex to D. Compose with the sheafified q to obtain e, a quasi-isomorphism.

Each finite projective term is a retract of a finite free A-module. Tilde and chart restriction transport that splitting to a finite free structure-module on Y. Thus each term is quasi-coherent and finitely presented. On an affine open U its section module is a finite projective Gamma(U,O)-module, hence flat. If U is contained in an affine V, Gamma(U,O) is flat over Gamma(V,O), and transitivity proves the required sectionwise flatness with the canonical restriction action. This includes rank zero and the zero ring.
